name: San Juan
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching San Juan: litigation and asset research, financial entity diligence, contractor vetting and Spanish records.
hero_lede: San Juan is the seat of Puerto Rico's government, courts, banks and international financial entities, and the hub of a metro area that generates most of the island's output. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating Puerto Rico-licensed detectives and counsel.
intro: San Juan is the capital of Puerto Rico and the centre of the San Juan-Carolina-Caguas metropolitan area, home to about 2.05 million people in 2024. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York estimates that the San Juan metro accounts for roughly 75 per cent of the island's economy. Hato Rey's Golden Mile concentrates banks, law firms and professional services, while Old San Juan, Condado and Isla Verde support government, tourism and hospitality. The port handles cruise traffic and a large share of the island's imported goods, and Luis Munoz Marin International Airport sits in neighbouring Carolina. Retail, health care and education employ the most metro residents, and the island's economy has grown faster than the US mainland in recent years after nearly two decades of decline.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to San Juan because so much of Puerto Rico's money, litigation and public spending passes through the city. Investors and relocating individuals operating under the island's tax incentive regime typically establish offices or residences in the metro area, and counterparties need to verify what they represent. Reconstruction funding since Hurricane Maria and the island's debt restructuring have generated large public contracts and complex federal and Commonwealth litigation. Banks and international financial entities headquartered in the city need diligence on clients and partners. Law firms need party, witness and asset research in Spanish-language Commonwealth records alongside federal dockets.

matters.title: Verifying relocated investors and executives
matters.text: Individuals and businesses relocating to the San Juan area for tax incentives often present themselves as established investors. We verify identity, business history, litigation, regulatory actions and adverse media across mainland and Puerto Rico records before clients commit to partnerships, investments or senior appointments.

matters.title: Reconstruction and public contract diligence
matters.text: Recovery and infrastructure spending administered from San Juan has drawn many contractors and subcontractors. We research ownership, related parties, prior performance disputes, debarment and exclusion records and political connections for prime contractors, lenders and oversight bodies assessing integrity and capacity.

matters.title: Financial entity counterparty reviews
matters.text: Banks, international financial entities and fintech firms based in San Juan serve clients across Latin America and the mainland. We profile owners, directors and principal clients, review regulatory and litigation history and flag indicators of nominee arrangements, shell structures or reputational risk for compliance teams.

matters.title: Asset research for creditors
matters.text: Judgment creditors and bankruptcy trustees pursuing San Juan-based debtors need a picture of real estate, companies and other interests. We search the Commonwealth corporate and property registries, court records and federal bankruptcy dockets and map connected entities on the island and the mainland.

matters.title: Hospitality and real estate transactions
matters.text: Hotels, short-term rentals and condominium developments in Condado, Isla Verde and Old San Juan attract investors from outside the island. We examine sponsors, sellers, title history, permitting disputes and litigation to support buyers, lenders and joint venture partners in the transaction.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in San Juan
local_context.text: The Court of First Instance has a San Juan Judicial Region whose Superior Court hears civil and commercial cases arising in the municipality, generally in Spanish. The Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico also sit in San Juan. The US District Court for the District of Puerto Rico sits in the city and hears federal cases in English, including the island's debt restructuring proceedings under PROMESA, making its docket central to many financial investigations.

local_context.title: Detective licensing and visiting investigators
local_context.text: Fieldwork in San Juan requires a private detective licensed under Puerto Rico law, administered through the Puerto Rico Police. The law also allows a detective licensed in another US state or territory to be authorised temporarily by the Superintendent for a specific mission, free of charge. In practice we coordinate Puerto Rico-licensed detectives, who know local procedures, records and Spanish-language sources.

local_context.title: Financial regulators in the capital
local_context.text: The Office of the Commissioner of Financial Institutions (OCIF), which supervises banks, international financial entities and other licensed financial businesses, is based in San Juan, as are the main Commonwealth agencies administering tax incentive decrees. Regulatory orders, licence lists and enforcement actions from these bodies are useful sources when assessing financial counterparties and decree holders based in the city.

local_context.title: Registries and property records
local_context.text: Companies are registered with the Puerto Rico Department of State, whose online registry is searchable island-wide. Real estate in San Juan is recorded in sections of the Property Registry of Puerto Rico, part of the Department of Justice, which follows a civil law registration model in which title, mortgages and liens are entered by property. Searches therefore need the property's registry details, and municipal records may supplement them.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in San Juan and works on San Juan matters from Nashville. We start by defining the question with the client and counsel, whether verifying a relocated investor, vetting a reconstruction contractor, reviewing a financial counterparty or supporting litigation in the Court of First Instance or the federal court. We then identify which Commonwealth and federal records apply, working in Spanish and English and connecting island records with mainland sources. Where interviews, site visits or surveillance are required, we coordinate Puerto Rico-licensed private detectives. We do not use pretexting or access restricted databases, and reports separate verified facts from indications.

faqs.q: Can a mainland-licensed investigator work in San Juan?
faqs.a: Puerto Rico law allows a detective licensed in another US state or territory to receive temporary authorisation from the Superintendent of Police for a specific mission. In most engagements we instead coordinate Puerto Rico-licensed detectives, who are familiar with local records, procedures and Spanish-language sources. Counsel can advise on which route suits a particular matter.

faqs.q: Are San Juan court records in Spanish?
faqs.a: Commonwealth courts, including the Superior Court in San Juan, generally conduct proceedings and issue filings in Spanish, while the US District Court for the District of Puerto Rico operates in English. We review records in both languages and provide English summaries or translations of key documents so clients and mainland counsel can rely on them.

faqs.q: Can you verify someone who has relocated to San Juan for tax incentives?
faqs.a: Yes, through lawful public sources. We confirm identity and history across mainland and Puerto Rico records, review litigation, regulatory actions, business affiliations and adverse media, and check for publicly available information on incentive decrees. Confidential tax information is not public, so we note where verification depends on documents the subject must provide.

faqs.q: How are property searches handled in San Juan?
faqs.a: Real estate is recorded in the Property Registry of Puerto Rico, which registers title, mortgages and liens property by property rather than by owner name alone. Effective searches therefore need registry details for each property. We combine registry research with court, corporate and municipal records to build an accurate picture of holdings.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in San Juan?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is headquartered in Nashville and has no office, staff or address in San Juan or elsewhere in Puerto Rico. We handle San Juan matters through scoped consulting engagements, coordinating Puerto Rico-licensed private detectives and working alongside the client's counsel where local work is required. We do not provide legal advice.
